Unit 23 – Grammar

Relative clauses / participles · 10 exercises · Click a tab to start

Exercise A – Circle the correct word
Choose the correct relative pronoun or adverb for each sentence.
  • 1. The minister, was appointed just last week, made no comment on the situation.
    ✓ who (refers to a person; non-defining relative clause)
  • 2. Isn't that the spot the accident happened last night?
    ✓ where (refers to a place)
  • 3. The human brain, weighs about 1400 grammes, is ten times the size of a baboon's.
    ✓ which (refers to a thing; non-defining)
  • 4. There are several reasons I don't want to see Michael tonight.
    ✓ why (reason why = relative adverb for reason)
  • 5. This is the office I work.
    ✓ where (place where I work)
  • 6. The new girl in our class, name is Alexandra, seems really nice.
    ✓ whose (whose = possessive relative pronoun)
  • 7. The Titanic, people said was unsinkable, sank on her maiden voyage.
    ✓ which (non-defining relative clause — cannot use 'that' in non-defining)
  • 8. All the people to the e-mail was sent replied.
    ✓ whom (object pronoun after a preposition: to whom)
  • 9. April 1st, we play tricks on people, is known as April Fools' Day.
    ✓ when (refers to a time; non-defining)
  • 10. Harry Hill, new series starts next week, is one of my favourite comedians.
    ✓ whose (whose new series = possessive)
  • 11. A very popular breed of dog is the German Shepherd, is often used as a guard dog.
    ✓ which (refers to a dog/thing)
  • 12. Blackpool Tower, was modelled on the Eiffel Tower, is a very well-known landmark.
    ✓ which (non-defining relative clause — must use which, not that)
Exercise B – Tick (✓) if correct; rewrite if incorrect
If the bold relative word is correct, write ✓. If incorrect, write the correct word.
  • 1. November 5th was the day which Guy Fawkes tried to blow up Parliament.
    ✓ when (the day when = time relative adverb)
  • 2. There were none of my favourite biscuits left when I had a cup of tea, that was really annoying.
    ✓ which (non-defining clause referring to the whole situation — cannot use that)
  • 3. I've just got a new webcam that takes really clear pictures.
    ✓ Correct (defining relative clause with 'that' for a thing)
  • 4. The Godfather was made by Francis Ford Copolla, who's daughter is also a film director.
    ✓ whose (possessive: whose daughter)
  • 5. Can you think of any reason which Cathy should be angry with me?
    ✓ why (reason why)
  • 6. Here's a photo of the hotel where we stayed in when we were in Beijing.
    ✓ Correct (where = place)
  • 7. How do you think the first man whom walked on the moon felt?
    ✓ who (subject position — who walked, not whom)
  • 8. This is the first occasion on which the leaders of these two countries have met.
    ✓ Correct (on which = formal relative after preposition)
  • 9. He is a person for who very few people feel much sympathy.
    ✓ whom (after a preposition: for whom)
  • 10. The moment which the hero suddenly appears from behind a tree is the best moment in the whole film.
    ✓ when (the moment when = time relative)
  • 11. I met a man which had a dog with only three legs.
    ✓ who (refers to a person)
  • 12. My new school, who I moved to about a month ago, seems like quite a friendly place.
    ✓ which (refers to a school/thing, not a person)
Exercise C – Rewrite as one sentence using a relative clause
Combine the two sentences into one using an appropriate relative clause.
  • 1. My friend, Simon, plays the guitar. He has just released a CD.
    Example given: My friend, Simon, who has just released a CD, plays the guitar.
    ✓ My friend, Simon, who has just released a CD, plays the guitar.
  • 2. Prince Charles is heir to the throne of England. His wife was Princess Diana.
    ✓ Prince Charles, whose wife was Princess Diana, is heir to the throne of England.
  • 3. Microsoft has a lot of power in the world of computers. That annoys some people.
    ✓ Microsoft has a lot of power in the world of computers, which annoys some people.
  • 4. The euro replaced a number of national currencies. It was introduced in January 2002.
    ✓ The euro, which was introduced in January 2002, replaced a number of national currencies.
  • 5. Friends ran for ten years. It is one of my favourite series.
    ✓ Friends, which ran for ten years, is one of my favourite series.
  • 6. Venus is a very hot place. It is much closer to the Sun than the Earth is.
    ✓ Venus, which is much closer to the Sun than the Earth is, is a very hot place.
  • 7. Cricket is popular in many countries around the world. It is played between two teams of eleven.
    ✓ Cricket, which is played between two teams of eleven, is popular in many countries around the world.
  • 8. Parts of Buckingham Palace are open to the public. It is where the queen lives.
    ✓ Buckingham Palace, where the queen lives, is open to the public in parts.
  • 9. The greyhound is the fastest dog. It can reach speeds of over 65 kilometres an hour.
    ✓ The greyhound, which can reach speeds of over 65 kilometres an hour, is the fastest dog.
  • 10. 1984 was written by George Orwell. His real name was Eric Blair.
    ✓ 1984 was written by George Orwell, whose real name was Eric Blair.
Exercise D – Write one word in each gap (do not use that)
Complete the passage with one relative word in each gap. Do not use 'that'.
Find me a show that works

I'm sure there was a reason (1) I became a TV reviewer. Maybe it was my love of classic shows (2) kept me entertained as a child. Or maybe it was the presenters (3) seemed to promise an exciting world of glamour and showbiz. To be honest, I've watched so many shows lately (4) have bored me to tears that I've forgotten. Take Kid Swap, for example, the new show (5) Channel 7 hopes will revive their viewing figures. The show takes kids (6) parents have had enough and swaps them with kids from other families for two weeks. The problem with this show is that I'm just not sure at (7) it's aimed – parents or teenagers. Parents (8) watch this show will find it childish, particularly at the moment (9) one of the teenagers does nothing but complain. Teenage viewers (10) watch more than the first five minutes will soon get bored of the parents, (11) blame anybody but themselves for the situation. This is definitely one idea (12) should be put exactly where it belongs – in the bin!

✓ (1) why  (2) which  (3) who  (4) which  (5) which  (6) whose   (7) whom  (8) who  (9) when  (10) who  (11) who  (12) which
Exercise E – Can 'that' be used?
For each gap in Exercise D, write ✓ if 'that' could also be used there, or ✗ if it could not.
  • 1. Gap 1 (reason ___):
    ✗ (reason why — 'that' not used with 'reason why' here)
  • 2. Gap 2 (classic shows ___):
    ✓ (defining relative clause — 'that' can replace 'which')
  • 3. Gap 3 (presenters ___):
    ✓ (defining relative clause — 'that' can replace 'who')
  • 4. Gap 4 (shows lately ___):
    ✓ (defining clause — 'that' can replace 'which')
  • 5. Gap 5 (new show ___):
    ✓ (defining clause — 'that' can replace 'which')
  • 6. Gap 6 (kids ___ parents):
    ✗ ('whose' is possessive — 'that' cannot replace 'whose')
  • 7. Gap 7 (at ___):
    ✗ ('that' cannot follow a preposition: at that — not standard)
  • 8. Gap 8 (Parents ___):
    ✓ (defining clause — 'that' can replace 'who')
  • 9. Gap 9 (moment ___):
    ✗ ('when' refers to time — 'that' not interchangeable here)
  • 10. Gap 10 (Teenage viewers ___):
    ✓ (defining clause — 'that' can replace 'who')
  • 11. Gap 11 (parents, ___):
    ✗ (non-defining clause after comma — 'that' cannot be used)
  • 12. Gap 12 (one idea ___):
    ✓ (defining clause — 'that' can replace 'which')
Exercise F – Choose the correct answer
Choose the best option A, B, C or D to complete each conversation.
  • 1. 'Who's that over there?' 'Oh, it's our new teacher, ………… just started work today.'
    ✓ D who (refers to a person; defining or non-defining OK)
  • 2. 'Which CD did you get Marcus in the end?' 'I got him the one ………… said he really wanted to hear.'
    ✓ A that (defining relative clause: the one that he said…)
  • 3. 'Who did you send a Valentine's card to?' 'I'm not telling you, but it was someone ………… name begins with "B".'
    ✓ C whose (possessive: whose name)
  • 4. 'Have you seen Jason Green's latest film?' 'Is that the one in ………… joins the FBI?'
    ✓ D which (in which he joins… — preposition + which)
  • 5. 'Why do you like Tania so much?' 'Well, she's one of the few people to ………… I can really talk.'
    ✓ B whom (to whom I can talk — preposition + whom)
  • 6. 'Why don't we go to Lionel's for dinner tonight?' 'Is that the new restaurant ………… has just opened on the other side of town?'
    ✓ C where (the restaurant where… = place)
  • 7. 'Could you lend me some money?' 'I'd like you to give me one good reason ………… I should.'
    ✓ B why (reason why I should)
  • 8. 'What do you want to do this summer?' 'I think we should go somewhere ………… has plenty of sun and sand.'
    ✓ B where (somewhere where = place relative adverb)
Exercise G – Circle the words in bold which are NOT necessary
Some bold relative words can be omitted (contact clauses). Mark which ones are unnecessary by writing their number below.

The number of options (1) that are available to us with (2) which to fill our leisure time is increasing all the time. While previous generations, (3) who lived before the electronic age, had musical instruments and card games (4) that they played to pass the time, we have PlayStations, computers, televisions and stereos. Although parents (5) whose teenagers spend a lot of time on these activities might worry about the effect (6) which it is having on them, for most of us they provide harmless fun, (7) which is becoming more important as life becomes more stressful. The television programmes (8) which we watch and the computer games (9) that we play all entertain us and, although there will always be people to (10) whom they seem a complete waste of time, the effect (11) that they have on society cannot be ignored. Entertainment is something (12) which we all need and, as long as we're willing to pay, there will always be someone (13) who is willing to provide it.

Which numbered words are unnecessary (can be omitted)? Write the numbers separated by commas:

✓ Unnecessary (can be omitted): 4, 6, 9, 11, 12 (object relative pronouns in defining clauses can be dropped)
Exercise H – Circle the correct word or phrase
Choose the correct participle form in each sentence.
  • 1. Before Harriet, I never knew what real love was.
    ✓ meeting (before + -ing gerund; subject of main verb also did the meeting)
  • 2. I'm sure that after your exam, you'll feel a lot better.
    ✓ passing (after + -ing; same subject)
  • 3. Having the letter, Peter printed it out.
    ✓ finished (Having + past participle = perfect participle for completed action)
  • 4. through the window, I saw a strange man at the door.
    ✓ Looking (active participle: I was looking through the window)
  • 5. I cooked dinner and, that, I sat down to watch TV.
    ✓ having done (perfect participle for action completed before the next)
  • 6. a noise outside, Janice went to investigate.
    ✓ Hearing (active participle: Janice heard a noise)
  • 7. my notes, I couldn't revise properly for the test.
    ✓ Having lost (perfect participle; lost before revising)
  • 8. quite intelligent, Matt hopes to get into a good university.
    ✓ Being (present participle for general/ongoing state — not a completed action)
  • 9. the start of the film, I decided not to bother watching the rest of it.
    ✓ Having missed (perfect participle; missed start before deciding)
  • 10. After her bed, Cherie had a shower.
    ✓ making (after + -ing; active participle)
Exercise I – Complete so that the meaning remains the same
Complete the second sentence using the participle clause given, so it means the same as the first.
  • 1. I suddenly remembered where I'd left my keys when I was waiting for the bus.
    Waiting
    ✓ Waiting for the bus, I suddenly remembered where I'd left my keys.
  • 2. I slipped because I was trying to run in the rain.
    Trying
    ✓ Trying to run in the rain, I slipped.
  • 3. I felt quite sorry for Tim when I saw him cry.
    Seeing
    ✓ Seeing him cry, I felt quite sorry for Tim.
  • 4. John was depressed because he knew he was going to fail the exam.
    Knowing
    ✓ Knowing he was going to fail the exam, John was depressed.
  • 5. The reason I'm quite good at basketball is that I'm quite tall.
    Being
    ✓ Being quite tall, I am quite good at basketball.
  • 6. Georgia didn't know any Japanese so she used a phrase book when she was there.
    Not
    ✓ Not knowing any Japanese, Georgia used a phrase book when she was there.
  • 7. Ed can afford three holidays abroad each year because he has a lot of money.
    Having
    ✓ Having a lot of money, Ed can afford three holidays abroad each year.
  • 8. Maria began to worry when she realised she was lost.
    Realising
    ✓ Realising she was lost, Maria began to worry.
Exercise J – Extra word: tick (✓) or write the extra word
If a line is correct, write ✓. If there is an extra word, write it.
Easy Money – TV Game Show
1 'Hello, viewers, and welcome to Easy Money, the game show who you
2 voted the best on TV! Now, remember yesterday when our current champion,
3 Pat Barber, having been won ten thousand euros, decided to carry on? Well,
4 she's here tonight and she's going for the star prize, which it is a brand new
5 sports car! That's right. Having got her this far, if Pat can answer three more
6 questions correctly, then she could be driving home in this car, ladies and
7 gentlemen. Having not seen the programme before, you will know just how
8 difficult which it can be. I know Pat's a little nervous, but I'm sure she'll be
9 fine and there's one person for whom tonight is very special and that's Pat's
10 husband, Frank, who he is sitting in the audience. So, let's play Easy Money!
